messages:
maya: heads up — since 06:12 UTC I'm seeing the HPA kick pods from 6->12, CA spins up 3 GPU nodes, but most pods stay Pending for >90s while the nvidia driver + image pull finish. CA then scales down because pods still unschedulable? we end up with 2x churn

jurgen: ugh we've hit that before. logs? kube-scheduler events? could be the init-containers or kubelet driver install blocking scheduling.

maya: pasted snippet:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----     ------            ----   ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled         2m     default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/runner-abc to gke-redwood-gpu-1
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m     kubelet            node didn't have required resources: nvidia.com/gpu
  Normal   Pulling           1m30s  kubelet            Pulling image "gcr.io/redwood/llm-runtime:prod"
  Normal   Started           1m     kubelet            Started container init-driver
```
Looks like nodetools taint/toleration dance and driver init before device plugin registers.

maya: CA logs show repeated scale up for same pending pods:
Scaler: will consider 3 nodes; reason: 9 pending pods require nvidia.com/gpu
Scaler: scale up complete: added 3 nodes
Scaler: no node group for new demand; removing 2 nodes (scale down)
```

ops-bot: alert: cluster-autoscaler detected frequent scale events (3 in last 12m). Throttling notifications. :rotating_light:

sri: two things to try quickly: 1) add a small warm pool of prebooted GPU nodes with taint: key=warm, effect=NoSchedule and a toleration on llm pods so they can use them when needed; 2) increase HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds and/or use metric smoothing for our external GPU-queued metric.

toa: +1 on stabilizationWindow. Also consider increasing pod startupProbe timeout — some of our init-driver work takes ~60s on preemptible instances after node boot. If the pod is marked Unhealthy it can trigger restarts and worsen churn.

jurgen: another approach: annotate pods so CA doesn't treat them as immediately evictable during boot: `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/skip-taint=true`? (we use a custom CA build for that). Or set `--max-node-provision-time` higher.

maya: we don't run a custom CA; but we can change `--scale-down-unneeded-time` and `--scale-down-unready-time`. currently scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, scale-down-unready-time=5m. Might be too aggressive.

sri: also watch VPA — I noticed VPA is recommending much smaller CPU requests for the init container which leads scheduler to pack pods and later HPA spikes because of CPU throttling. VPA + HPA interactions are messy when VPA evicts/recommends in the background.

maya: example VPA recommendation: `requests.cpu: 0.05 -> 0.02` for init-loop. Not ideal.

toa: quick mitigation: add annotation to disable VPA for LLModel pods: `vpa.kubernetes.io/update-mode: "Off"` until we stabilize autoscaler.

jurgen: long-term: we should implement a GPU warm pool in a separate node pool with labels like `node.k8s.io/gpu-warm=true` and a minimal daemonset to pre-load OCI layers and driver modules, then use a CA expander policy to prefer those nodes. That reduces image pull + driver init latency to <10s.

maya: agree. also thinking about external metrics: our HPA is driven by `external/prometheus-llm_pending_queue` which is very spiky. We should use Prometheus recording rules to smooth with a 2m avg: `avg_over_time(queue_total[2m])` and feed that to the HPA adapter.

jurgen: good call. smoothing prevents transient bursts from triggering multiple scale ups. And set `behavior` on HPA: `scaleUp: policies: - type: Percent, value: 100, periodSeconds: 60` and `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 180`.

sri: also add a pod-level toleration for warm pool and a nodeSelector for critical inference jobs so low-priority batch pods don't get the warm nodes. Use PriorityClass to prefer inference over lower jobs.

maya: will try three quick changes in this order: 1) disable VPA updates for the LLModel namespace, 2) switch HPA metric to smoothed recording rule, 3) bump CA scale-down thresholds to avoid premature shrink.

toa: FYI, for BZ we might also want to pre-pull OCI images via DaemonSet with `ImagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` on warm nodes. saves ~20-40s.

maya: deployed HPA metric change and VPA annotation. CA config change scheduled for next maintenance window. Observing now.

kube-alerts: notice: pending_pods metric decreased from 14 -> 3 within 6m after HPA smoothing deployed.

maya: neat, looks better already. will follow up tomorrow with proposal for warm nodepool + prepull daemonset + node boot tuning. thanks all :thumbsup:

jurgen: add plan to infra backlog and tag the cost impact (warm pool adds baseline GPU cost). we can evaluate using small B-series preemptible GPUs as warmers.

maya: filing a short RFC in #eng-infra-docs with cost tradeoffs.

toa: if we do warm pool, consider using spot+taints so we can scale to on-demand if insufficient capacity in a region.

maya: noted. end thread.
